Cc: contracts@nimblehealth.com
Date: 2026-05-27T15:04:00Z
Subject: Order form commercial questions and a couple of redlines

Kimberly — thanks for the call today. We reviewed the Order Form + MSA redlines with our procurement and legal teams. Two quick asks that would unblock us on our side: 

1) Net terms: procurement is pushing for Net-45 rather than Net-30. They'll accept Net-30 if we can allow invoicing at month-end and a 15 business day processing window on their side — can Redwood accommodate Net-45 for the initial 6 months and then revert to Net-30 thereafter?

2) Tax and entity: our tax team needs the invoice to be issued to NimbleHealth UK Ltd for EU usage and NimbleHealth Inc for US usage. We attached the tax certificate for the UK entity. Are you able to support split invoicing by region/entity, or do invoices need to come from a single Redwood entity?

I've attached our annotated redlines to the Order Form (highlights on pricing ladder and minimum-commit language). If you can loop in finance and legal to confirm the above, we can provide final sign-off.

Thanks — Sara
Sara Jenkins
Head of Procurement, NimbleHealth

Sara — appreciate the clear summary and the attachments. Looping in Ben (commercials) and Marissa (finance) — and Karthik from legal to confirm MSA alignment. Quick responses below and next steps: 

- Net terms: We can make Net-45 an interim option for the first 6 months if we capture that in the Order Form appendix (auto-revert clause). Ben, can you confirm language and whether this affects the pricing ladder trigger?

- Split invoicing by legal entity: Redwood can issue invoices from Redwood Inc (US) or Redwood Ltd (UK) depending on the billing entity on the signed order — but we generally require a single billing entity per order. If Nimble wants regional split invoices, we'll need a dual-entity order and an exhibit that maps usage buckets to entities. Marissa, can your team confirm operational feasibility and any minimum dollar thresholds for split invoicing?

Next steps:
- Ben to propose a short appendix for the Net-45 interim clause (target: EOD 5/29).
- Karthik to review the MSA redlines that Sara attached and flag any conflicts with our standard tax/gross-up clauses (target: 5/31).
- I'll set a 30-min alignment with Nimble's procurement and our finance ops to finalize routing/PO workflow. Sara — are you ok with a Wed 5/29 10:00 PT slot?

Thanks,
Kimberly Park
Sr. Commercial Counsel (Contracts)

Kimberly / Sara — quick note on the pricing ladder and minimum commit impact: 

If we add an interim Net-45 clause (auto-revert after 6 months), it doesn't change the published unit rates, but it does affect the trigger timing for minimum commitment true-ups. We should add a clause that ties the true-up measurement to 'billing periods' rather than 'payment receipt' to avoid a timing mismatch. Draft language I suggest: 

"For the purposes of minimum commitment measurement, consumption will be measured on an invoice-period basis independent of agreed payment terms. Any shortfall true-ups will be invoiced following the applicable invoice schedule."

On split invoicing: Finance (Marissa) — the operational burden is moderate but doable if Nimble can provide separate POs per legal entity and maintain usage segregation. We also need to confirm tax withholding obligations for the UK invoices; Karthik, can legal confirm whether the tax certificate supplied is sufficient for exemption?

I attached a one-page appendix draft (inline in the attached redline doc) and highlighted the billing-period phrasing. Will iterate once Karthik and Marissa confirm.

Ben Carter
VP, Commercials — Redwood Inference
Attachment: Nimble_OrderForm_redline_v4.docx (contains appendix draft)
From: karthik_iyer@redwood.example

Cc: ben_carter@redwood.example, marissa_cole@redwood.example, Sara Jenkins <sara.jenkins@nimblehealth.com>
Date: 2026-06-01T11:28:00Z
Subject: RE: Order form commercial questions and a couple of redlines

Team / Sara — I reviewed the attached redline and the tax certificate. Notes and recommended positions: 

1) Net-45 interim: acceptable with the auto-revert language. Drafted a short clause to be inserted in the Order Form appendix stating "Interim Net-45 for first six (6) months post-Effective Date; thereafter Net-30 unless otherwise agreed in writing." That is commercially reasonable and limits long-term exposure.

2) Measurement for minimum commit: I agree with Ben's billing-period approach. We should avoid tying true-ups to payment receipt. Legal will accept the proposed phrasing with one tweak: change "invoice-period basis" to "invoice cycle period (as defined in Appendix A)" so we can later define cycles per entity if split invoicing is adopted.

3) Split invoicing and tax: the UK tax certificate looks standard and should support nil VAT treatment if Nimble provides a valid VAT registration and the activity qualifies. Operationally, split invoicing is okay provided: (a) Nimble supplies a PO for each Redwood billing entity and (b) usage can be segregated by region/workspace. If Nimble cannot segregate usage, dual-entity invoicing is not feasible. 

Action items: 
- Kimberly: please circulate a revised Order Form with the drafted appendix and the revised measurement phrasing.
- Marissa: confirm whether Redwood Finance can accept two POs under the same deal with separate remit-to entities and whether our AR system needs an exception ticket.
- Sara: please confirm whether your procurement team can provide separate POs and whether the UK entity will register usage separately.

I'll mark legal as "approve pending finance operational confirmation."

Karthik Iyer
Senior Counsel, Redwood Inference
